summary: An excerpt from a fiction novel (labeled Book 2, part 181) in which the antagonist Dawna tells Rio that she and her colleagues have decided to kill him because he proved a liability rather than an asset to their research. Dawna says she will only incapacitate him with a Taser and have a troop finish the job, and she describes him as a fascinating research subject. When she fires the Taser, Rio collapses, and the narrator, after Arthur's gun hand twitches, knocks Arthur unconscious with an elbow strike and keeps Dawna in view.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, Dawna has decided to kill Rio as a failed research subject, but the narrator intervenes by knocking out the armed Arthur.
key_facts: Dawna tells Rio that her colleagues deemed his lack of success in harnessing his power indicative, and that he is a liability with too little potential for turning to an asset.
Rio says, "In simpler language, you are going to kill me."
Dawna says she will not kill Rio herself because she does not have the stomach for such acts.
Dawna retrieves a Taser from one of the fallen troops in the doorway.
Dawna says Mr. Tresting is otherwise occupied and that convincing Ms. Russell to do it would take more time and energy than they have.
Dawna says, "I will not be sorry for your death," and calls Rio's death far less than he deserves.
Dawna describes Rio as "a most fascinating subject of research" and says the recruitment efforts failed in his case.
Dawna tells Rio, "I regard it as something of a personal failure that our recruitment efforts have failed in your case."
Rio agrees the recruitment efforts failed "Quite spectacularly so."
Dawna fires the Taser at Rio, who jerks, stiffens, and collapses.
Arthur's gun hand twitches, and the narrator notes the movement is far enough for the narrator to act on.
The narrator slips to the side and smashes an elbow into Arthur's temple, and Arthur crumples.
The narrator's finger stops half a millimeter from firing the gun.
Dawna is gazing at the narrator, fearless and searching, while Rio lies prone and forgotten at her feet.
